# Bike sales analysis

I have conducted sales analysis of a Kaggle [dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sadiqshah/bike-sales-in-europe) which contains orders for the bicycle store. They sell different products for sport lovers that fall into categories like Bikes, Accessories, and Clothing. You can find everything starting from Socks and Gloves, ending with Hydration Packs and Fenders. They operate in France, United States, Australia, Germany, United Kingdom, and Canada. The timeframe of the dataset is 5.5 years (from Jan 2011 to Jul 2016).

## **Data preparation and cleaning** 

This step aims to prepare the dataset for further analysis by removing duplicates, and handling missing data.

The dataset comprises 113,036 rows and 18 columns before cleaning. All of the columns have no missing data.

| Column | Description  | Data type | Missing values | Example values  |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **date** | The date order was made | date | 0 | 2011-01-01 |
| **day** | The ordinal number of the day in month | int | 0 | 31 |
| **month** | The name of the month order was made | text | 0 | November |
| **year** | Year of the order | int | 0 | 2015 |
| **customer\_age** | Age of a customer | int | 0 | 19 |
| **customer\_gender** | Male or Female | text | 0 | M, F |
| **age\_group** | Age group to which customer belongs | text | 0 | Adults (35-64) |
| **country** | The country in which order was made | text | 0 | Canada |
| **state** | State in which sale occured | text | 0 | British columbia  |
| **product\_category** | The category of a product | text | 0 | Accessories |
| **sub\_category** | Subcategory of a product | text | 0 | Bike Racks |
| **product** | Name of the product | text | 0 | Hitch Rack \- 4-Bike |
| **order\_quantity** | Order quantity | int | 0 | 8 |
| **unit\_cost** | Cost per unit | int | 0 | 45 |
| **unit\_price** | Price per unit | int | 0 | 120 |
| **profit** | Profit made from order | int | 0 | 590 |
| **cost** | Total cost for the order | int | 0 | 360 |
| **revenue** | Revenue made per order | int | 0 | 950 |

### Handling profit, cost, and revenue columns miscalculations 

The profit column for the first 10 entries shows wrong values according to the standard business formula: **Profit \= Revenue \- Cost**.

Revenue and cost also should be recalculated:

* **Revenue \= order\_quantity \* unit\_price**  
* **Cost \= order\_quantity \* unit\_cost**

I assumed that other entries also had wrong values, so I recalculated all of them and saved the resulting view as ***ProfitRecalculated***.

## **Performing analysis**

### Temporal analysis 

First let’s start by analyzing how profit changed from month to month over years. 

![][image1]

We can see local highs occurred in December. This indicates seasonality. People tend to spend more during Christmas holidays. 

* As we can see from the chart above profit stayed within a corridor for the **first 2.5 years (between 240K and 500K)**. This could be due to ineffective marketing or poor quality of products at that time.   
* After that it showed exponential upward move with local high at 1.5M in Dec 2013 **(growth of over 5 times compared to Jun 2013\)**. Something big happened. Maybe a launch of a new marketing campaign or new stores opened in other countries.   
* The profit remained high (above 1M) until Jun 2014\.  
* In Jul 2014 a **major drop occurred (-77%)**. The post‑Christmas rush has calmed down.   
* Between Jun 2015 and Dec 2015 profit spiked again to its **ATH** of 1.9M (**over 4 times growth since Jun 2015**).   
* **Major drop** after Jun 2016\.

The overall chart indicates highs during Christmas periods and major drops in post-holidays periods. 

### Customer segmentation by age group

Now we should find out what our potential customer looks like in terms of age.

![][image2]

* **Adults** represent half of our profit by customer age distribution. We should target this age group in our marketing and sales strategies. This might be due to the fact that after 35, many people feel they’ve accomplished what they wanted in their careers and want to enjoy life and leisure more. That is why they buy bicycle accessories and bikes.   
* **Young adults** represent 35.7%. People of this age enter a maturity stage of their career development and start to buy more products for their future ‘more relaxed’ life.   
* **Youth** (13.9%). In that age we often concentrate on our studies and career. This leaves less time for personal life, so we do not need bikes or other products for leisure.  
* **Seniors** tend to spend time on calm activities that do not include much physical load. That is why they represent only 0.4%

Not much to say. We should target each group equally.

### Regional segmentation 

We should take a look at the geographical profit distribution across our network. 

![][image4]

United States: 32.9%

Australia: 25.9%

United Kingdom: 11.5%

Germany: 10.4%

France: 10.2%

Canada: 9%

We should increase our presence in the UK, Germany, France and Canada as they account only for 41% of our total profit distribution. The US and Australia account for 59% which is centralized.

### Segmentation by product category 

Bikes: 66.30%

Accessories: 24.77%

Clothing: 8.93%

Bikes are our primary product category. We should center our sales and marketing strategy around it. First advertise the bike to a customer and then some accessories that would supplement the main purchase. 

### Distribution of profit by subcategory within bikes category

Our main customer base is about sporty bikes \- road ones. They love speed and want to look fit. We should keep that in mind while developing marketing and sales strategy. Emphasize the bike's lightness, stiffness, sharp handling and so on.
